item.description: Venture capital (VC) funding in Egypt grew by 31% year-over-year (YoY) in the second half of 2025 (excluding December), hitting $524 million raised from 71 deals.

item.title: How rising fuel costs launched Nigeria’s first EV-only assembly plant
item.description: Nigeria’s fuel subsidy removal sent petrol prices soaring and forced a rethink of how people move goods and people. In that shock, electric vehicles shifted from a fringe idea to an economic case, opening the door for Nigeria’s first electric-only vehicle assembly plant.

item.title: The Antigua gambit goes bust: The mobility shortcut that African nomads just lost
item.description: For years, Caribbean citizenship let Nigerian entrepreneurs and globally minded professionals move easily between markets without leaving home. Antigua and Barbuda’s passport was a mobility hack, opening doors in Europe and easing US visa scrutiny. Now, Trump’s new restrictions on Caribbean citizenship programmes, specifically on Antigua and Barbuda and Dominica, tighten that access, forcing professionals to rethink how they navigate global opportunity and stay in motion.

item.title: Here is why bank transfers in Nigeria will cost more from 2026
item.description: From January 2026, sending ₦50,000 ($34.14) through your bank app could cost you ₦100 in transfer fees. Not because banks suddenly changed their pricing, but because the Nigerian government has changed who pays for electronic transfers.
